contracts.authorization: Anonymous read-only GET. It grants no session, credential, configuration, payment or account authority.
contracts.idempotency: The query is read-only and returns an equivalent static declaration for repeated and concurrent requests.
contracts.compatibility: Version 1 is a closed response. New fields, capability names or schema versions require a new versioned contract before server and client changes.

inputSchema.description: No request body or query fields are accepted by the bootstrap declaration.

outputSchema.description: Closed desktop bootstrap recognition response v1.

success.description: Indicates that the static bootstrap declaration was returned successfully.

data.description: The complete closed desktop bootstrap declaration for contract version 1.

schema_version.description: The closed response schema version understood by the desktop client.

service.description: Stable service identifier used only for desktop bootstrap recognition.

contract_id.description: Stable identifier for this exact bootstrap contract.

minimum_client_version.description: Minimum desktop client version allowed to recognize this contract, expressed as strict three-part semantic versioning.

capabilities.description: Explicit capability declarations; every future integration remains disabled in this release unit.

device_authorization.description: Whether a governed device authorization flow is available.

account_read.description: Whether authenticated account projection is available.

usage_read.description: Whether account usage projection is available.

models_read.description: Whether the desktop model catalog contract is available.

pricing_read.description: Whether authoritative desktop pricing projection is available.

tool_keys_manage.description: Whether desktop tool-key management is available.

observability.correlation: No user or request correlation is emitted because this static anonymous query creates no operation.
observability.audit: No persistent audit record is created; normal HTTP access logging may record only the route and transport metadata under existing server policy.
observability.metrics: Existing generic route metrics may count requests; the contract exposes no customer or capability-use metric.

errorSemantics: Unsupported methods are not accepted and never change state.
The handler returns no secrets, account data, raw configuration or capability URLs.
Every future capability remains false until a separately governed implementation exists.

contracts.authorization: Anonymous read-only GET. It grants no credential; it only advertises implemented routes and current Redis-dependent availability.
contracts.idempotency: Read-only; equivalent requests return an equivalent capability and route declaration for the same server configuration.
contracts.compatibility: V2 is additive beside immutable v1. Clients below minimum_client_version must not activate it.

inputSchema.description: No body or query parameters are accepted.

outputSchema.description: Desktop v2 capability and route declaration.

device_authorization_available.description: Whether Redis-backed device authorization is currently available.

account_read.description: Existing authenticated account projection is available.

usage_read.description: Existing authenticated usage projections are available.

models_read.description: Existing account-scoped model projection is available.

tool_keys_manage.description: Existing authenticated token management is available.

official_usd_cny_rate.description: Fixed comparison exchange rate confirmed by the product owner.

observability.correlation: Existing HTTP request correlation applies; the response contains no user identifier.
observability.audit: No persistent audit record is created by this read-only declaration.
observability.metrics: Existing route metrics may count calls without recording secrets.

errorSemantics: The route remains available when Redis is unavailable and declares device_authorization_available false.
The v1 response is never mutated.

contracts.authorization: Anonymous POST with the existing anonymous body-size and rate-limit middleware; unavailable unless Redis is configured.
contracts.idempotency: Each successful call creates a distinct five-minute authorization; retries create a new code and do not reuse prior codes.
contracts.compatibility: V2 only; values are opaque and clients must honor expires_in and interval.

inputSchema.description: Optional bounded desktop client display name.

client_name.description: Display name shown on the approval page.

data.description: Opaque device code and human verification data.

verification_uri_complete.description: First-party approval page with user code only.

interval.description: Minimum initial polling interval in seconds.

observability.correlation: Request correlation excludes device_code and user_code.
observability.audit: No database audit row; approval is represented by Redis state and the eventual user_session.
observability.metrics: Count outcome codes only, never authorization values.

errorSemantics: Redis absence or failure returns service_unavailable without a code.
Generation failure leaves no partial Redis key pair.

contracts.authorization: Authenticated live browser user_session only; PAT credentials cannot approve a desktop device.
contracts.idempotency: A repeated identical decision returns the existing status; a conflicting later decision is rejected.
contracts.compatibility: V2 only; decision is a closed approve or deny enum.

inputSchema.description: Human code and explicit browser decision.

observability.correlation: Existing authenticated request correlation applies without logging user_code.
observability.audit: The eventual user_session records desktop_device; denied and expired codes leave no database row.
observability.metrics: Count approved, denied and expired outcomes only.

errorSemantics: Unknown or expired codes return a closed error and do not create a session.

contracts.authorization: Anonymous POST authenticated by the high-entropy device_code; pending exchange is rate limited and successful exchange is one-time.
contracts.idempotency: Pending polls are safe; one approved code can create at most one user_session. A lost successful response requires a new authorization rather than replaying a refresh secret.
contracts.compatibility: V2 only; clients handle authorization_pending, slow_down, access_denied, expired_token and already_used codes.

outputSchema.description: Dedicated desktop access and refresh credentials.

refresh_token.description: Rotating refresh secret stored only by the desktop credential vault.

observability.correlation: Existing request correlation applies; credential values are excluded from logs.
observability.audit: Successful exchange creates the existing user_sessions row with login_method desktop_device.
observability.metrics: Count pending, slow-down, denied, expired, used and issued outcomes without values.

errorSemantics: Polling too quickly returns slow_down and a retry interval.
Denied, expired and consumed codes never issue credentials.

contracts.authorization: Possession of the rotating desktop refresh token and matching session_id.
contracts.idempotency: Existing user_sessions refresh rotation and bounded replay window apply.
contracts.compatibility: V2 JSON transport reuses existing session semantics without cookies.

observability.correlation: Existing authentication correlation applies without token logging.
observability.audit: Existing user_sessions last-active and rotation state remain authoritative.
observability.metrics: Existing auth outcome metrics apply without token values.

errorSemantics: Invalid, expired, revoked, mismatched or reused refresh tokens return the existing closed authentication error codes.
A failed rotation does not expose a replacement secret.

contracts.authorization: A live desktop bearer access token backed by user_sessions; PAT credentials are rejected.
contracts.idempotency: A session can be revoked once; later access is unauthorized.
contracts.compatibility: V2 route reuses existing session revocation semantics and does not delete API tool keys.

observability.audit: The existing user_sessions row records revoked state and reason desktop_logout.

errorSemantics: PAT or missing session credentials are forbidden.
Revocation never deletes or changes tool keys.
